analysis.title: Weekly Market View: Increasing signs of a bottom
key_insights: Democrats won the US Senate and House in the mid-term elections. The bank sees three implications: policy gridlock likely stalls fiscal expansion and new tariffs, a prolonged Middle East conflict becomes less likely (lowering oil prices and inflation expectations), and the pace of AI data-centre buildout is at risk (curbing AI-linked bond supply).

Democrats also flipped governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas, giving them a majority of the 50 state governorships for the first time since 2010. Higher corporate and wealth taxes are a long-term risk if Democrats win the 2028 presidential election.
Portfolio stance is a mid-cycle playbook: broadly balanced across assets while looking for tactical opportunities. Global equities were trimmed to Core last week.

With the VIX above 25, the bank sees rising signs of an equity market bottom. It adds an opportunistic idea on US IT after a 17% quarterly correction and uses elevated volatility to earn income through structured strategies.

Oil fell 12% over the past week. The bank sees the geopolitical risk premium fading, with oil easing towards USD 80/bbl over 6-12 months. Oil-driven disinflation should let central banks adopt less aggressive policies.

US IT fell 17% this quarter. Past quarterly declines of about 20% (Q4 2008, Q2 2022, Q4 2018) were followed by average returns of 5.1% in the next quarter, 14.8% over two quarters and 46.5% over four quarters. Semiconductors, about 40% of US IT, fell more than 30% since the bank closed its opportunistic idea a month ago and look oversold.

Semiconductors are under pressure on concerns about data-centre moratoria. Beneficiaries of Democrat policies include clean energy (including solar), defensives, affordability-related stocks, tariff-rollback beneficiaries and healthcare (Medicaid-related names).

The bank still expects two more Fed hikes by H1 2027 given sticky near-term inflation and a robust economy, then cuts in H2 2027 as cheaper oil lowers inflation. Markets now price two additional 25bps hikes by H1 2027, down from three. Ultra-long yields stay elevated on fiscal concerns.

The bank prefers the 3-7-year part of the DM yield curve and BBB-to-BB-rated credit for income. Slower data-centre construction could reduce hyperscaler issuance, but some data-centre-focused deals could become less viable, so it is cautious on lower-quality issuers. CCC-rated debt has reached distressed levels.

The bank expects a modestly weaker USD over 6-12 months and a range-bound dollar near term. Democrat control of Congress limits tariff escalation, fiscal expansion and rapid AI buildout, which supported the USD. DXY support is at 100.7. Gold is supported by a softer dollar and central-bank buying led by China.

Q3 US earnings: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat estimates as of 30 October, but the aggregate beat was only 4.5%, smaller than recent quarters. Q3 earnings growth is 31.6% y/y, with expected growth of 36.1% in 2026 and 16.4% in 2027. Slower upgrades suggest the bull market is maturing. Big Tech capex remains high and free cash flow is expected to stay negative.

The bank is Overweight US and Asia ex-Japan equities. It is Overweight the US IT, US healthcare, US financials, US materials, Europe ex-UK financials and Japan financials sectors. It expects equity returns of 8-10% annually in mid-cycle (mid-to-high single digits in another section), using 2015-17, when S&P 500 returned 8.3% annually under an opposition Congress, as the comparison.

Japanese banks: the BoJ's September hike to 1.25% should show in the December quarter as loans reprice. The bank expects three further BoJ hikes by June 2027 and is positive on the sector, favouring strong deposit franchises and room for higher shareholder returns.

India upgraded to Overweight within Asia ex-Japan equities. Foreign investors sold USD 32bn year to date while domestic institutions bought USD 74bn. The Nifty 50 one-year forward P/E is 18% below its long-term average, ROE is 14.7%, and the bank expects 14-15% earnings growth in 2027 versus 29% for AxJ.

US 2- and 10-year yields are expected to range 4.5-4.75% and 5-5.25% over three months. Twelve-month forecasts are 4.25-4.5% and 4.75-5%. A much stronger payrolls print that pushed markets to price a third hike is the main risk for the 2-year yield.
GBP: the BoE hiked 25bps to 4% as expected and GBP was little changed. The bank expects EUR/GBP to rebound towards 0.8450, as the ECB holds a tightening bias and UK fiscal policy is tighter.

AUD: the RBA hiked to 4.85% but AUD lagged because the hike was priced at 88% and the bank dropped its reference to further increases, with three members preferring a hold. The bank is bullish on AUD/USD, targeting 0.72 in three months and 0.74 in 12 months, and would add on pullbacks.

Weekly macro balance: the bank judges the week negative for risk assets near term. Positives were robust US manufacturing and job openings and potential easing of geopolitical tension. Negatives were weak China PMIs, BoE and RBA hikes, and a recalibration of the AI trade.

Table of US IT declines: Q4 2008 -22.0%, Q2 2022 -19.8% and Q4 2018 -17.4%, averaging -19.7%, followed by 5.1% in the next quarter, 14.8% over the next two and 46.5% over the next four. Q4 2026 stands at -17.0%.
Table of S&P 500 annualised returns by cycle: early cycle 2009-2015 19.1%, mid-cycle 2015-2017 8.3%, early cycle 2023-2027 20.5%, and mid-cycle 2027-2029 unknown.
vol_and_positioning: VIX is above 25, which the bank reads as a rising sign of an equity market bottom. It recommends using elevated volatility to earn income through structured strategies.
The US tech sell-off spread to global equities and triggered margin calls, weighing on AUD.
Market diversity indicators (fractal dimension) show investor diversity has normalised: Global Equities 1.47, MSCI US 1.50, Global Bonds 1.93. Values below 1.25 signal a high risk of reversal.
S&P 500 technicals as of the 5 November close: spot 7,354, first support 7,188, first resistance 7,682, 12-month forward P/E 17.8x.
geopolitical: Democrats' win limits President Trump's ability to prolong the Iran conflict. Vice President Vance and Republican leaders blamed the defeat on the Iran conflict, and Democrat control of the defence budget from next year constrains escalation.
President Trump said a deal with Iran 'could happen' amid intensive talks and repeated no immediate plan for a wider attack.
Houthis claimed fresh drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's airports.
Trump said the US was close to a trade deal with Canada.
Democrats called for an AI development pause and a superintelligence ban.

tension_points.bull_case: US IT fell 17% this quarter and semiconductors more than 30% in a month. Past sharp declines were followed by strong returns, and IT earnings growth remains solid with AI monetisation and cloud growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic control and state-level wins in Texas and Georgia raise the risk of data-centre moratoria, which could reset AI capex expectations. Big Tech free cash flow is under pressure and buildout is increasingly debt-funded.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant reset in data-centre spending expectations, for example through moratoria in leading data-centre states.

tension_points.bull_case: Two hikes are already priced, oil-driven disinflation should allow cuts in H2 2027, and long-end yields should be less sensitive to a single payrolls print.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky near-term inflation and a robust economy, with JOLTS at 7.52mn and jobless claims near three-month lows, could lead markets to price a third hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significantly stronger-than-expected payrolls print that leads markets to price a third hike.
